evidence.text: Xu Shen glosses 肉 as 胾肉 and classifies it as pictographic. The received annotation interprets 胾 as a large piece of animal meat and says 肉 was extended to the body of a ring-shaped object and to the “flesh” of music. These are dictionary explanations, not independently dated attestations of each sense.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary entry and later annotation
evidence.title: 肉 ròu - 漢典

evidence.text: The entry gives citations for meat and bodily flesh from transmitted works including Zuǒzhuàn, Mèngzǐ, Xúnzǐ, Mòzǐ, and Zhànguócè, but does not establish the date of the cited wording or the earliest use of each sense. It separately lists fruit pulp with a citation from 齊民要術 and the ring-body sense with citations from 爾雅 and 漢書 commentary. These should not be collapsed into a single chronology from the modern gloss list.
evidence.title: 肉 ròu - 漢典
